_meta.label: PUBLISHED, NOT REPRODUCED BY US
_meta.description: Claims and figures for BDH / BDH-GPU taken directly from the original paper. Nothing in this file was measured, re-run, or verified by our project's own pipeline. Use only for side-by-side context next to our own precomputed KV-cache results (see accuracy_vs_budget.json), never merge the two into one chart without this disclaimer.

source.title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain

claims.claim: BDH-GPU empirically matches GPT2-architecture Transformer performance on language and translation tasks at equal parameter counts.
claims.conditions: Same training data as the Transformer baseline it is compared against.
claims.quantitative_value_note: Paper reports this as a qualitative parity/scaling-law claim ('rivals GPT2-architecture Transformer performance'); it does not give a single headline number (e.g. one perplexity delta) that applies across the whole 10M-1B range, so no single number is recorded here to avoid misrepresenting the source.

claims.claim: BDH-GPU often learns faster per training token than the comparable Transformer baseline.
claims.quantitative_value_note: Reported qualitatively in the paper's summary of results; no single 'X% faster' figure is given in the abstract-level material we sourced.

claims.claim: BDH activation vectors are sparse and positive by construction (a property of the ReLU-lowrank feed-forward block in BDH-GPU), and the model demonstrates monosemanticity — individual synapses that reliably strengthen when the model processes a specific concept.
claims.quantitative_value_note: Our project's diagram plan uses an illustrative '~5% neuron activation per token' figure for the sparse-activation visual; that specific percentage is our own placeholder for the demo, not a number taken from the paper, and must not be presented as a published result.

claims.claim: Experiments in the paper cover parameter counts from 10M up to 1B; no results are reported above 1B parameters.
BDH-GPU, as a state-space reformulation, has no fixed context-length limit, unlike a standard fixed-context Transformer.
claims.source_location: Architecture description (BDH vs. BDH-GPU vs. Transformer)

claims.claim: BDH-GPU uses fewer parameter matrices than a comparably-sized Transformer.
claims.quantitative_value_note: No specific matrix count or ratio was available in the source material we reviewed; recorded as a qualitative architectural claim only.

claims.claim: The brain-correspondence claims (macro-to-micro correspondence between Transformer attention and observed brain attention mechanisms) are presented by the authors as a theoretical/empirical hypothesis, explicitly not a proven biological mechanism.

explicitly_not_included: Any perplexity, BLEU, or benchmark table values — the source material reviewed for this file did not surface a machine-readable results table; only qualitative 'rivals GPT2' framing was available. Do not backfill these with estimated numbers.

Sudoku/reasoning-benchmark comparison numbers shown in the project's GitHub README (github.com/pathwaycom/bdh) — those come from a separate follow-up evaluation, not the arXiv paper itself, and would need their own citation if used.
